served.stem: A researcher raises the outside glucose concentration step by step and measures how fast glucose enters a muscle cell. Uptake rises at first, then levels off at a maximum rate. What does that plateau tell you?
choices: Glucose is entering by simple diffusion straight through the lipid bilayer
The cell has begun pumping glucose back out at an equal rate
Glucose crossing has switched over to active transport
The membrane became impermeable to glucose at high concentration
The carrier proteins are saturated, so transport has a ceiling
served.bankWhy: A plateau is the fingerprint of a finite number of protein binding sites. Simple diffusion climbs in a straight line with the gradient because there is nothing to fill up, while a carrier has a limited number of seats, and once every seat is occupied, adding more glucose cannot speed anything up. Curve flattens means protein involved, whether the transport is facilitated or active.

answer.text: The carrier proteins are saturated, so transport has a ceiling
answer.line: A plateau means a limited number of something. Here every glucose carrier is busy, so the rate cannot climb.

steps: Look at the shape. Uptake rises, then flattens at a maximum.
A ceiling means a fixed number of something. Here it is the glucose carriers, the GLUT proteins.
Once every carrier is busy, more glucose outside cannot speed anything up. Simple diffusion would keep climbing in a straight line.

choices.text: Glucose is entering by simple diffusion straight through the lipid bilayer
choices.note: Simple diffusion climbs in a straight line with concentration and never levels off. The plateau points the other way: to proteins.

choices.text: The cell has begun pumping glucose back out at an equal rate
choices.note: Nothing in the data shows glucose leaving. An outflow equal to the inflow would bring net uptake to zero, not hold it at a maximum.

choices.text: Glucose crossing has switched over to active transport
choices.note: Active carriers saturate too, so a plateau does not show a change of mode. Glucose entering down its gradient needs no energy.

choices.text: The membrane became impermeable to glucose at high concentration
choices.note: Membranes do not switch off at high concentration. Uptake holds at its maximum; it does not drop to zero.

choices.text: The carrier proteins are saturated, so transport has a ceiling
choices.note: Every carrier busy: the rate hits its ceiling.

student.lockIt: A curve that levels off means saturated carrier proteins; a straight line means simple diffusion.
student.hook: Limited seats, so the rate tops out.
